        # directly into the script — a changed_files output is built from
        # real filenames in the diff, and interpolating one straight into
        # `run:` would let a filename containing quotes/shell syntax break
        # out of the assignment and execute on the runner (zizmor:
        # template-injection). Reading from env avoids that entirely.
        env:
          ALL: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_all_changed_files }}
          HOMEPAGE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_homepage_all_changed_files }}

Instead I ran all 5 angles myself sequentially, treating each as an independent investigative pass (separate falsification attempts, separate evidence), and cross-checked where they intersected (Angle 3's suppression-logic finding and Angle 4's broken-E2E finding turned out to be the same story from two ends). Flagging this since the task explicitly asked for a fan-out. --- ## Angle 1 — Test coverage depth Ran both files for real: ``` ✓ overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.test.tsx (8 tests) 22ms ✓ overrides/app/components/product-view/colourSwatches/index.test.tsx (19 tests) 191ms Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 27 passed (27) ``` - **🔴 Pagination logic (PAGE_SIZE boundary, chevron clicks, disabled states, both page-management `useEffect`s) has zero Vitest coverage.** `colourSwatches/index.test.tsx:54` (`const THREE = [...]`, 3 variants) — every one of the 19 tests uses ≤3 variants, so `PAGE_SIZE=4` (`index.tsx:28`) is never crossed. The auto-advance-to-selected-colour's-page effect (`index.tsx:119-125`, the deep-link `?color=` case) and the shrink-clamp effect (`index.tsx:128-130`) are exercised by **neither** Vitest nor Storybook — I read all 7 stories and all 19 tests; none ever sets a selected/initial value at an index ≥ `PAGE_SIZE`. CONFIRMED. UNIFORM risk (state-machine effect with no seeding fixture — exactly the class of bug the task's "React logic correctness" guidance warns about). - **🟡 `colourSwatches/index.test.tsx:29-31`'s comment is false, CONFIRMED by direct reproduction.** It claims `test-storybook` "currently fails on every story in the repo," so play functions are "unverified until CI." I built Storybook and ran the real test-runner locally: ``` PASS colourSwatches/index.stories.tsx — 7/7 (incl. SevenColours pagination play) PASS footer/index.stories.tsx — 6/6 PASS ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.stories.tsx — 23/23 ``` All green, real headless-Chromium runs, no env fault reproduced. This matters because it's the stated justification for *why* Vitest doesn't duplicate pagination coverage — and that justification doesn't hold today. ONE-OFF (comment-level). - **🔴 AC4 (URL updates via `?color=`) has zero test coverage anywhere.** No `product-detail/index.test.tsx` exists (only the pre-existing, unrelated `productInfo.test.ts`). `handleColourSelect`/`colourVariants`/`selectedColour`/`hasOfferedColour` (`product-detail/index.tsx:262-307`) is entirely untested by Vitest, and the one E2E scenario written for it can't run (see Angle 4). CONFIRMED. - **Mutation falsification, done for real, both survived:** removing the `currentIndex === -1` special case (`index.tsx:152-157`) and falling through to modulo (`(-1-1+3)%3=1` → Bravo) would fail the "ArrowLeft... lands on the LAST swatch" test's assertion (expects Charlie) — real, non-tautological. Mutating `sizedSwatchUrl` to always use `?` would break the `&`-separator test's exact-match assertion. Both clean, not inflated. - `staticProductHeader.test.tsx`'s `compareDocumentPosition` bit-4 check (line 94) is a real assertion — a swapped render order flips the bit and fails `.toBeTruthy()`. Clean. ## Angle 2 — Contract fidelity, `filterImageGroups.ts` - **🔴 The file's own justification for existing is false, CONFIRMED.** `filterImageGroups.ts:2-6` claims the base path "is an internal module with no public export." But `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:182` has `export const filterImageGroups`, the package has no `exports` field restricting deep imports, and — this PR's **own** touched files already import two sibling functions from that identical path: `product-view/index.tsx:73` (`getPriceData`) and `product-detail/index.tsx:26` (`getUpdateBundleChildArray`), both `from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'`. The correct import was two lines away in the same file. DRY violation compounded by a misleading comment. UNIFORM risk (same false-justification shape could recur for any other base utility). - **🟡 Real behavioural divergence, CONFIRMED by executing both implementations side by side** (verbatim transcriptions, not paraphrase): ``` BASE with null imageGroups -> no throw, result: undefined JHOAN with null imageGroups -> THREW: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'filter') BASE values:null -> THREW: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'find') JHOAN values:null -> no throw, result: [] ``` Base uses `imageGroups?.filter(...)?.filter(...)` (survives explicit `null`); Jhoan's version (`filterImageGroups.ts:42`) has no optional chaining there and relies solely on a default parameter, which doesn't catch `null`. (Jhoan's version is *more* defensive on the `values: null` case — this isn't one-directionally worse, just genuinely different from what the header comment claims to replicate.) Mitigated today because the one call site (`product-detail/index.tsx:289`) pre-guards with `?? []`. Should-fix the comment and/or add the same guard for future callers. - **🔴 No test file exists for this utility** — confirmed via `find`. It has 2 conditional filters, a `throw`, and a destructure-with-fallback — squarely inside conventions.md's "Vitest required when ≥1 conditional branch" rule. ## Angle 3 — Security / failure modes - `sizedSwatchUrl` and `handleColourSelect`'s `URLSearchParams`-based construction: clean, CONFIRMED no injection risk (auto-percent-encoding, `data:` short-circuit, falsy `imageUrl` already filtered upstream). 🔵 one low-value theoretical note: a URL with a `#fragment` before any `?` would get `?sw=...` appended into the fragment rather than as real query params — no evidence real SFCC swatch URLs carry fragments, not pursued further. - **🔴 The headline finding of this review.** `product-detail/index.tsx:905`: `suppressColourAttribute={hasOfferedColour}`. `hasOfferedColour` (`product-detail/index.tsx:307`) is `false` in two *different* cases: (a) no colour attribute exists at all, and (b) a colour attribute exists but every value was filtered out by AC5 — exactly the PR's own Gherkin scenario "A product whose colours are all unavailable shows no colour section at all." I traced case (b) through three files: `product-view/index.tsx:797-801`'s base loop only skips `id === 'color'` when `suppressColourAttribute` is true; the `variationAttributes` it iterates comes from `useDerivedProduct` → base `getDecoratedVariationAttributes` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:218-239`), which I confirmed decorates **every** value unconditionally with no orderable/image filtering at all. So when every colour is AC5-withheld, `suppressColourAttribute` is `false`, the base loop is **not** skipped, and it renders its own unfiltered `variant="square"` swatch group showing every colour AC5 says must be hidden entirely — directly contradicting AC5 and the dedicated Gherkin scenario. CONFIRMED via full static trace across the three files; not clicked through live (no matching product fixture available), and the one E2E scenario written to catch exactly this is itself non-functional (Angle 4) and no Vitest/Storybook test touches this wiring either — so nothing in the delivered test suite would catch it. `suppressColourAttribute` should almost certainly be gated on `colourVariants.length > 0`, not `hasOfferedColour`. - 🔵 minor, PLAUSIBLE only: `colourAttr.values.map(...)` (`product-detail/index.tsx:288`) would throw if `values` were a malformed non-array truthy value — not SDK-typical, low priority, same generic SDK-trust posture as the rest of the codebase. ## Angle 4 — E2E quality - **🔴 PR body's claim ("all 11 scenarios skip") is false, CONFIRMED by execution.** `e2e/fixtures/products.js` (untouched by this PR) exports only `standardProduct`, `multiVariantProduct`, `outOfStockProduct`, `saleProduct` (line 77) — none of the 5 new fixtures the spec imports (`pdpProductWithMultipleColours`, `pdpProductWithUnpopulatedColour`, `pdpProductWithNonOrderableColour`, `pdpProductWithSingleColour`, `pdpProductWithAllColoursWithheld`) exist anywhere in the file. Reproduced directly: ``` pdpProductWithSingleColour: undefined THROWS: TypeError: pdpProductWithSingleColour is not a function ``` This throw happens on the line *before* `test.skip(!sku, ...)` in 10 of 11 tests — they'd **error**, not skip. The 11th (`standardProduct`, no skip guard at all) would actually attempt to run for real. - **🔴 Independently fatal: `e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js` defines none of the ~10 colour-related Page Object members the spec calls** (`colourLabel`, `colourSelectedName`, `colourSwatchGroup`, `offeredColourNames()`, `selectedColourSwatch`, `colourSwatch()`, `colourValueFor()`, `selectColour()`, `focusColourSwatches()`, `colourSection`). Confirmed by reading the full file (32 lines) plus `BasePage.js`, and by grepping the entire `e2e/` tree — these identifiers appear **only** inside the spec file itself. The diff added exactly one trivial line to `ProductPage.js` (`this.productDescription = ...`). Even with fixtures fixed, every test fails immediately on first locator access. The spec as delivered is fully non-functional, not "correctly deferred." - Gherkin/spec **design** is otherwise solid — one behaviour per scenario, explicitly load-bearing assertions (e.g. checking a *named* withheld colour is absent, not just a count; a `window.__sfcc91NoReload` flag proving no full reload). Would likely catch real regressions once the plumbing is fixed. - Tags: `{tag: ['@pdp', '@SFCC-91']}` applied uniformly, matches feature file and testing.md format. Clean. - **🟡 `pdp` has no allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes`** — only `e2e_homepage` exists (line 108); `Compute E2E scope` (lines 137-171) hardcodes its subset check to `$HOMEPAGE` only. Any develop-PR diff touching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` resolves to `e2e_scope=skip`, confirmed by tracing the script — same gap as the parallel build. 🔵 tangential: lines 55-60's comment ("falls back to the full suite") contradicts lines 121-136's comment and the actual code (line 167 sets `skip`) — pre-existing doc drift in Tier-1 CI config, not this PR's fault, noted since I was reading the exact section anyway. ## Angle 5 — `generateRegistry.mjs` - **Clean, CONFIRMED via full-codebase A/B execution.** Built a byte-identical "old behavior" copy (single line reverted: `body = normaliseBody(blockMatch[3])` → `body = blockMatch[3]`), ran both against all 101 `.ts`/`.tsx` files under `overrides/app/` (30 with a `Props` block). Exactly **one** file diverged — `product-view/index.tsx`, the intended fix target, where the old algorithm mangled `validateOrderability`'s multi-line type into 4 broken fragments (silently dropping `product: SfccProduct` entirely) and the new one correctly collapses it. All other 29 files: byte-identical output. Strong evidence this is a safe, non-regressive fix. - **🟡 But the new comment/quote scanner doesn't track template literals (backticks), CONFIRMED by reproduction.** A synthetic prop block with a backtick string containing an unbalanced `(` causes the next unrelated prop to be silently swallowed and vanish from the registry entirely: ``` extractTsProps result: ["testId?: `prefix-(${string}`; label?: string"] // 1 prop, not 2 — "label" lost ``` Doesn't affect any of today's real files (per the sweep above), but directly undercuts the fix's own stated goal for one of TypeScript's three quoting syntaxes. Latent, not live. UNIFORM concern for shared tooling. - Entry-point guard (`fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1]`) is the correct standard ESM idiom; traced all four branches (direct-run-with-arg, direct-run-no-arg, imported-with-arg, imported-no-arg) — preserves old direct-execution behaviour while suppressing the side effect that would otherwise fire on `generateRegistry.test.mjs`'s `import`. Clean. ## Supplementary checks explicitly requested - **Circle→square, other callers:** grepped every `.stories.tsx`/`.test.tsx` for `variant="circle"` and scanned `bonus-product-view-modal`, `use-bonus-product-selection-modal`, `product-item`, `cart` for any square/circle reference — **zero matches**. No existing test would have caught this global change. Also searched this PR's 7 commit messages and `.docs/` for any Figma/PRD citation of a square-swatch decision — none found. CONFIRMED: undocumented, uncaught. - **`alt=""` always-safe check:** re-read `colourSwatches/index.tsx` and `index.stories.tsx` in full — there is exactly one `` (line 260), always inside the `role="radio"`/`aria-label` button (lines 242-270); no other rendering path exists.
